text: Time to run every piece of this chapter together, on one real dataset: a stage, a file format, and COPY INTO, in a single sitting.
Step one is the destination, not the source. Before loading anything, the target table has to exist — and Snowflake confirms it was created before you move on.
Then prove the source side. LIST at-stage shows the real files sitting in a real public S3 bucket — not a guess about what should be there.
The real test is whether the two sides actually match. Twelve columns, in this exact order — the real dataset either lines up with the target table or it doesn't.

That's the whole chapter in five steps: an external stage pointed at the public bucket, a named file format with the CSV rules, a target table matching the dataset's columns, and a COPY INTO with ON_ERROR set on purpose, not left at the default.

Verifying the load reuses the same load metadata from Lesson 14. Counting the rows once, then re-running the exact same COPY INTO, should load zero additional rows — proof the skip-already-loaded behavior works on a real file set.
Next chapter: Snowpipe. Everything you just did by hand is about to run automatically.
